newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Sierra Leone militia threatens to march on Freetown.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone militia threatens to march on Freetown.

text.p: Members of a civilian militia loyal to Sierra Leone's ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on Wednesday vowed to march on the capital unless Nigerian troops restore him to the power he lost in last weekend's coup.

The new military rulers in Freetown ordered the Kamajors to disband and hand in their weapons, but militiamen in this Liberian border town near the Mano River Bridge crossing with Sierra Leone showed no sign of doing so.
Armed with rusty automatic rifles, shotguns, machetes, bows and arrows or spears, they chanted victory songs singing Kabbah's praises.
"We are awaiting word from President Kabbah and we will be in Freetown to help restore order and democracy," said Kamajor commander Eddie Massalay.
"We went to the polls and democratically elected President Kabbah and until his term is over, no one can remove him."

A group of junior officers led by Major Johnny Paul Koromah seized power on Sunday, saying they wanted to bring rebels of the Revolutionary United Front into government to end a civil war persisting despite November's peace accord.
One of the first acts of the new army rulers was to ban the Kamajors, upon whom Kabbah had come to depend in battles against the rebels.

There have been clashes between Kamajors and the Sierra Leone army, and many soldiers resent the resources they have received from the presidency. The deputy defence minister in the ousted government, Hinga Norman, is a former Kamajor.
The border was open on Wednesday and troops of the Nigeria- led ECOMOG regional force are patrolling on the Liberian side.

The Kamajors said they welcomed a show of force by Nigeria, which sent hundreds of troops into Freetown to put pressure on the coup leaders to stand aside, provided its intention was to restore the elected government.
"Nigeria or ECOMOG is welcome in any part of Sierra Leone, provided their coming is to restore democracy. Bring back the president or we do it ourselves," Massalay said.
He said the Kamajors had been delighted to hear Kabbah speaking on BBC radio from Guinea, where he fled on Sunday.
"We want him back as soon as possible. We know no other president but Tejan Kabbah," he said.

On Tuesday police reported protests against the coup in Sierra Leone's southern second city of Bo, where Kamajors were ignoring an order to disband, and clashes between troops and Kamajors in the eastern garrison town of Daru.
